sense: a small part that shows what the whole is like

evidence: M-O s.v. sample (of product), after Vives
terms.comment: Its first sense, from eximere, to take out: what is taken out to show the rest (Lewis & Short). Its common senses are a copy, a pattern, a model to follow, an instance, and a warning to others (exemplum statuere in aliquem).

terms.gloss: a taste, a sample (of food, or of a writer’s work)
evidence: Plin. Ep. 4.27.5: Ad hunc gustum tōtum librum repromittō
Sen. Ep. 114.18: Gustum tibi dare voluī
terms.comment: A tasting, a taste; post-Augustan, not in Cicero (Lewis & Short). It is also the light first course of a Roman dinner, and taste as a sense (see taste).

phrases.latin: Vidēs quam ācūta omnia quam apta quam expressa. Ad hunc gustum tōtum librum repromittō
phrases.english: You see how sharp it all is, how neat, how vivid. On the strength of this sample I promise you the whole book is the same

phrases.latin: Gustum tibi dare voluī: tōtus hīs contexitur liber.
phrases.english: I wanted to give you a sample: the whole book is woven out of things like these.

sources: Lewis & Short: exemplum · Lewis & Short: gustus
